1a8b46d4-1333-46f3-99f8-90ab6491a4c9.title: OpenClaw Releases 2026.9.5 With Atomic Updates, Plugin Hot Reload, Conversation Sharing, and Expanded GPT Live
1a8b46d4-1333-46f3-99f8-90ab6491a4c9.incipit: OpenClaw is an open-source, MIT-licensed personal AI agent that you run on your own machines. Its Gateway connects models, tools, and chat channels such as Telegram, Slack, and Discord. The project has now...
1a8b46d4-1333-46f3-99f8-90ab6491a4c9.body: OpenClaw is an open-source, MIT-licensed personal AI agent that you run on your own machines. Its Gateway connects models, tools, and chat channels such as Telegram, Slack, and Discord. The project has now shipped version 2026.9.5 , announced on X . The release bundles 4,179 pull requests and 64 direct commits, with credits to 502 contributing accounts. The main change is Atomic Updates, which targets a long-running complaint: updates that break a working agent. Is it deployable? Yes, Version 2026.9.5 is the current latest tag on npm . It is self-hostable and needs Node 24.16+ or 26.1+. Why OpenClaw Updates Kept Breaking The OpenClaw team explained the problem in a blog post with maintainer Jason Sy . Before the fix, an update had 2 outcomes: incremental improvement or catastrophic failure. In the failure case, the old version went down as well. That left no agent online to help with the repair. Two factors made this hard. First, OpenClaw has thousands of config options, so testing every permutation is near impossible. Second, maintainers rarely felt the pain themselves. They are developers who ask Claude or Codex to update their claw. For many users, the claw is their only agent. The OpenClaw 2.0 launch in early September made the issue too large to ignore. How Atomic Updates Work According to the Claw team, the needed pieces already existed in the upgrade process. They were in the wrong order. The new flow works like this: The existing Gateway keeps running while the update is prepared. The next version is checked against a private copy of your setup. OpenClaw switches over, then verifies the updated installation. If the update fails, it rolls back to the last working configuration. OpenClaw always preserves a working agent, so it can help diagnose a failed upgrade. The team also added an issue reporting button for updates. The release notes list clear limits. Atomic Updates apply on supported update paths only. Rolling back the application cannot undo database migrations. The private validation copy is not a backup, so keep a verified backup before upgrading. If an interactive update fails, AI repair starts only after you choose Yes. It uses your account and tokens, and a 30-second timeout skips it. Interactive Explainer: OpenClaw 2026.9.5 What Else Ships in 2026.9.5 Plugin hot reload: you can install or reload supported plugins without restarting the Gateway. It works from the CLI or an authorized chat command. The CLI also accepts several plugins in 1 command. Conversation sharing: Session Share gives teammates on another paired installation read-only access to selected conversation groups. Recipients see conversation text and eligible forks. They do not see subagents, tool activity, or reasoning. Revocation cannot recall what was already received. Expanded GPT Live: you can speak while GPT Live replies in supported Meet, Teams, and Zoom meetings . It can consult your OpenClaw agent during meetings or phone calls . Live is audio-only, so the notes point to gpt-realtime-2.1 for camera use. Shared browser pages: a shared Browser dashboard lets you and your agent use the same page. It runs on a local OpenClaw-managed browser profile, not your laptop cookies. Conversation archiving: cold storage compresses older, inactive history. It is off by default and archives after 30 days once enabled. Reopening a conversation restores it and makes it searchable again. Specialist-agent setup: guided setup can create a chief of staff, researcher, writer, and reviewer. You can also pick a single specialist. Nothing is created before you approve the proposal. One upgrade warning applies to everyone. This release changes the conversation database even with archiving off. Going back requires the matching older build and a backup. How To Install or Upgrade New installs can use the official script: curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash If you already manage Node.js, install the published package: npm install -g openclaw@latest --allow-scripts=openclaw openclaw onboard --install-daemon Existing users can run openclaw update . See the updating guide for manual paths. The release also adds a FreeBSD CLI install route using system Node and npm. Key Takeaways OpenClaw 2026.9.5 ships 4,179 pull requests from 502 contributing accounts. Atomic Updates validate the next version while the current Gateway keeps running. Failed updates roll back, and a working agent stays available to diagnose. Plugins now install or reload without a Gateway restart. Back up first: rollback cannot undo database migrations. Michal Sutter Michal Sutter is a data science professional with a Master of Science in Data Science from the University of Padova. With a solid foundation in statistical analysis, machine learning, and data engineering, Michal excels at transforming complex datasets into actionable insights.

baf1ba73-becf-45de-9bec-1e717723d8c5.title: Apple Confirms iPhone 18 Battery Lithium Ion Silicon Carbon Samsung
baf1ba73-becf-45de-9bec-1e717723d8c5.incipit: https://www.forbes.com/video/e0d8ea2c-8311-4252-9210-8edf542bcf22/ Despite the company's rivals diving head-first into silicon carbon battery tech and the extra power it brings , Apple played it safe with good ol' lithium-ion batteries for the iPhone 18 range. Why it didn't go for the new battery tech makes sense, but
baf1ba73-becf-45de-9bec-1e717723d8c5.body: https://www.forbes.com/video/e0d8ea2c-8311-4252-9210-8edf542bcf22/ Despite the company's rivals diving head-first into silicon carbon battery tech and the extra power it brings , Apple played it safe with good ol' lithium-ion batteries for the iPhone 18 range. Why it didn't go for the new battery tech makes sense, but that doesn't mean Apple won't be tempted by the ultra-long battery life silicon carbon promises in the near future. The iPhone 18 Sticks Rather Than Twists Silicon-carbon batteries make a lot of sense, especially for foldable phones. They store significantly more energy in the same physical space as traditional lithium-ion cells, which is why Samsung used it in the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra this summer , fitting a 5000mAh cell into a thinner frame than the Fold 7 while adding 600mAh more. Samsung isn't stopping there. The Galaxy S27 Pro and Ultra will use silicon-carbon cells of approximately 5,200mAh and 5,700mAh respectively. The first time a Galaxy S phone has gone beyond 5000mAh. Chinese manufacturers are already going further. Xiaomi's Redmi Note 17 Pro Max ships with a 10,000mAh silicon-carbon cell. Apple's iPhone 18 Pro Max delivers up to 45 hours of video playback, which is Apple's longest ever battery life figure. But it achieves that through software efficiency, A20 Pro chip power optimisation and the C2 modem's 15% energy reduction and the new M16 OLED display, rather than a larger or more energy-dense cell. Apple has squeezed more from the same technology rather than adopting new technology. Imagine what it could do with a significantly denser silicon carbon battery. Why Apple Played It Safe With The iPhone 18 Battery The accepted wisdom for Apple, or any other electronics manufacturer avoiding silicon-carbon, is the cycle life trade-off. Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold 8 is rated for 1,200 charge cycles, compared to 2,000 on the Z Fold 7's conventional lithium-ion cell. A 40% reduction in rated longevity on paper looks bleak. But that's not the full story. A board member at a silicon anode materials supplier that works with smartphone manufacturers, and asked to remain anonymous, told me the cycle life comparison isn't the full picture. The silicon-carbon battery starts with roughly 20% more energy than conventional lithium-ion. If a user charges their phone to the same level each day, the silicon-carbon cell depletes to a shallower depth. This, he explained, effectively extends the real-world cycle count beyond the rated figure. The new Xiaomi 17 flagship smartphone is displayed alongside the Xiaomi Pad 8 Pro using silicon carbon battery technology. (Photo by Joan Cros/NurPhoto via Getty Images) By his calculation, a 1,200-cycle silicon-carbon battery used at 50% average daily depth reaches 80% of its original capacity after approximately 7.9 years. A 2,000-cycle lithium-ion battery reaches the same threshold after around 11 years. When the silicon-carbon battery hits 80% of its original capacity, it is still holding roughly the same charge as a brand new lithium-ion battery because it started 20% higher. "Whether it's 7.9 years or 11 years," he told me, "that's way longer than most people ever keep their phones." There is also a separate and more interesting question about Samsung's 1,200-cycle rating itself. The Galaxy S26 Ultra, which uses a conventional lithium-ion battery, is also rated at 1,200 cycles this year, down from the S25 Ultra's 2,000. If the reduced rating were purely a silicon-carbon trade-off, it would not apply to a lithium-ion device. The same source suggested this could reflect a different internal voltage model applied across Samsung's entire 2026 lineup rather than anything specific to the battery chemistry. "Batteries are the dark arts," he noted. None of which means Apple is wrong to wait. For Apple, the decision is less about cycle life maths and more about the reputational cost of a first-generation problem. An iPhone 18 Pro battery failure story is more damaging than a Galaxy Z Fold 8 battery story, because Apple's image is built directly on reliable hardware. Not just the latest and exciting tech. Apple prefers to be second with certainty than first with a footnote. Forget The iPhone 18, Will Apple Adopt Silicon-Carbon In 2027? The more likely candidate for Apple's first silicon-carbon deployment is the iPhone Air/2. Apple's ultra-thin device struggled because of poor battery life when it launched last year . A thinner phone needs a physically smaller battery, and silicon-carbon's superior density per millimetre makes the trade-off worthwhile when the alternative is poor battery life in a device marketed on thinness. It's also a somewhat experimental line for Apple, where mistakes might be forgiven more easily. If the iPhone Air 2 does come with a silicon carbon battery, don't be surprised if we see it deployed in the iPhone 19 too. iPhone 17 Price Slashed Further After iPhone 18 Price Hike Don't forget to subscribe to my free newsletter for instant deal updates, or follow my TikTok for more iPhone 18 news . This article was originally published on Forbes.com

ba03c45e-9025-4d71-9236-b34f04938114.title: OpenAI wants ChatGPT to be app store for AI
ba03c45e-9025-4d71-9236-b34f04938114.incipit: OpenAI yesterday launched a less expensive artificial intelligence (AI) model and tools that run continuously, as it aims to reposition ChatGPT as an app store for AI, AFP reported.Other...
ba03c45e-9025-4d71-9236-b34f04938114.body: SAN FRANCISCO — OpenAI yesterday launched a less expensive artificial intelligence (AI) model and tools that run continuously, as it aims to reposition ChatGPT as an app store for AI, AFP reported. Other companies, such as Adobe, will be able to offer their software directly within ChatGPT, which is now used weekly by 1.2 billion people. ChatGPT users will also be able to access their subscriptions in other apps. “We want to help people discover what you build and connect you with new customers,” OpenAI CEO Sam Altman told around 2,500 developers from around the world who gathered on the shores of the San Francisco Bay for the company’s annual conference. During his keynote speech, the 41-year-old executive made no mention of multiple security incidents that forced OpenAI to once again suspend development of some models on Friday, after one of its agents gained unauthorized access to the internet. Altman told reporters that “it is going to take us some time to figure out how to make sure that alignment, monitoring, safety, security stay well ahead of capabilities.” A new model unveiled yesterday, GPT-6.1 Sol, was described as almost as powerful as GPT-6 Astra at one-fifth the price. It comes one day after the company said it scrapped a new version of Astra because it often ignored instructions. Outside the conference, around thirty protesters shouted chants like “put people before profit,” alongside demands that OpenAI drop contracts with the US military and Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Inside, Altman rejected comparisons between the AI era and the Industrial Revolution. “I think we should learn from the mistakes of the Industrial Revolution, and I think we should be more like the Renaissance,” Altman said. That new renaissance is now increasingly connected to agentic software — or programs capable of automatically completing tasks like managing calendars, booking reservations and sorting through email. Attendees cheered the arrival of “dots” — OpenAI’s version of AI agents which will run continuously and ask users to approve sensitive actions. Dots will only be available to paid subscribers and are not yet available to individual users in the European Union, Switzerland and the United Kingdom due to regulations, though OpenAI hopes toresolve those issues. It competes with Meta’s Muse and Google’s Spark agents. Last week Meta unveiled a small Tamagotchi-like device powered by Muse that could ship by December. OpenAI is working on its own AI hardware but provided no updates. However, integrating the new dots onto a device “seems like a very reasonable thing to assume we may do someday,” Altman said. As speculation swirls around when OpenAI might go public, Altman told reporters yesterday that the company was “investing more in safety, security, alignment, monitoring, and that will allow us to continue to progress model capability a lot.” Despite gaining an early lead with ChatGPT, rival Anthropic overtook OpenAI in second-quarter revenue. Anthropic, which has focused more on business customers, generated US$11.6 billion (RM47.3 billion) dollars versus OpenAI’s US$6.7 billion, according to the Wall Street Journal. Meanwhile, Anthropic’s annual recurring revenue is expected to reach US$100 billion by the end of the year, while OpenAI reached US$70 billion in July, according to various reports. OpenAI has delayed its own Wall Street debut till next year at the earliest, as Anthropic aims for November. “I want OpenAI to be a public company someday,” Altman said, “but I don’t want to put additional pressure right now.” OpenAI is nonetheless seeking to raise at least US$30 billion from private investors in a deal that could increase its valuation to around US$1.4 trillion, up from US$852 billion in March, according to Bloomberg. Yesterday, OpenAI president and cofounder Greg Brockman attended an event at the White House where President Donald Trump said top AI executives agreed to a “morally binding” commitment to build AI with safeguards.

0fb1785a-bb82-457f-8f7c-0312401d6f87.title: Galaxy S27 Pro and S27 Ultra reportedly getting major battery upgrade
0fb1785a-bb82-457f-8f7c-0312401d6f87.incipit: Samsung’s Galaxy S27 Ultra and S27 Pro are expected to get major battery upgrades, with certification records pointing to typical capacities of about 5,700mAh and 5,200mAh, respectively. This would mark the most significant battery upgrade since the S20.
0fb1785a-bb82-457f-8f7c-0312401d6f87.body: Notebookcheck, edited Samsung's S27 series is expected to get its largest battery capacity jump since the S20 Ultra (pictured here). Samsung’s Galaxy S27 Ultra and S27 Pro are expected to get major battery upgrades, with certification records pointing to typical capacities of about 5,700mAh and 5,200mAh, respectively. This would mark the most significant battery upgrade since the S20. If the latest information proves true, Samsung’s Galaxy S27 Ultra will finally get its first major battery-capacity increase in several generations. Certification listings posted by China's 3C (China Compulsory Certification) show a Samsung SDI cell rated at 5,534 mAh (model EB-BS958DBY), which would translate to roughly typical capacity of 5,700mAh. This would represent about a 14% increase over the Galaxy S26 Ultra’s 5,000mAh battery and finally move beyond the capacity that Samsung has maintained since the Galaxy S20 Ultra . The Galaxy S27 Pro is also reportedly getting a substantial increase. Its battery is rated at 5,087mAh, corresponding to a typical capacity of around 5,200mAh. For comparison, the Galaxy S26 has a 4,300mAh battery, although the Pro and S26 are not directly equivalent models. Both new batteries will reportedly come with 60W wired charging, according to earlier certification listings . The figures are still based on leaked certification records rather than Samsung’s official specifications. Given Samsung’s increasing adoption of silicon-carbon battery technology, especially in the Galaxy Z Fold 8 series, these certification listings are certainly plausible. While earlier rumors have suggested substantially larger capacities, there is more agreement on the modest 5,534mAh figure for the Ultra. Again, Samsung is yet to officially announce the Galaxy S27 series or confirm these specifications. Jacob Fisher - Tech Writer / Translator - 3128 articles published on Notebookcheck since 2022 I first became acquainted with computers in my early teens after a broken leg from a football (soccer) match temporarily condemned me to a predominately indoor lifestyle. 00abc8f8-1b5e-451b-a45b-ff706c2eaa9f.title: ChatGPT Opens Its Sidebar to Outside Apps With Plugin Extensions and Event-Triggered Automations
00abc8f8-1b5e-451b-a45b-ff706c2eaa9f.incipit: ChatGPT plugin extensions bring outside apps into the sidebar and file viewers, while MCP events let connected apps trigger automations when something changes, with wider web access still on the way.
00abc8f8-1b5e-451b-a45b-ff706c2eaa9f.body: Plugins can now hook into more of ChatGPT’s own interface, including the sidebar and file viewers. At DevDay on September 29, 2026 , OpenAI opened “the platform we use to build ChatGPT features” to plugin developers. The new plugin extensions give an app a place in the sidebar , a panel beside your conversation, and its own viewer for file types it supports. A second change, MCP events , lets plugins start automations when something happens in a connected app. announced 29 Sep 2026 plans all Free, Go on web coming soon ChatGPT users 1.2B weekly The short version What plugin extensions add to ChatGPT How MCP events start automations Finding and building plugins FAQs The short version Plugin extensions let apps open in ChatGPT’s sidebar, in a side panel next to a chat, and as viewers for files. MCP events let a plugin trigger ChatGPT when something changes in a connected app, even while you’re away. Plugin Creator helps developers build plugins, and improved ranking helps people find them in the directory and in conversations. OpenAI lists all of this for every plan, but extensions on the web are still coming to Free and Go. OpenAI’s developer docs say extensions hook plugins into key parts of ChatGPT, including the sidebar, the composer and file viewers. Existing plugin features keep working as before. OpenAI’s DevDay recap shows Canva as a sidebar app. Where extensions can appear in ChatGPT Extension What you can do with it Sidebar apps Open an app from ChatGPT’s sidebar and use it full screen Conversation panels Open an app beside a chat, keeping the work and the conversation together File viewers and editors Open a supported file type in the app’s own interface and save changes there Plugin settings Change the plugin’s own settings without leaving ChatGPT Composer mentions Pick content from the plugin while typing a message (desktop app only) Rich forms Answer a plugin’s questions with richer inputs, such as choosing from images Extensions also let a plugin link straight to a page inside its sidebar app and share context both ways with ChatGPT. OpenAI’s Thibault Sottiaux (Tibo) wrote that developers “can now build full native apps with plugin extensions”, and that with “over 1.2B weekly users”, OpenAI “will surface relevant plugins right in the conversations”. Free and Go OpenAI’s recap says extensions are “available to all plans”. OpenAI’s developer documentation adds that extensions on the web are “coming soon to ChatGPT Free and Go users”, so Free and Go users don’t get them in a browser yet. Automations How MCP events start automations MCP events let ChatGPT subscribe to updates from a plugin, such as a new message, an edited document or a status change. You tell ChatGPT what to watch and what to do when it happens. The plugin then sends the event, and ChatGPT follows your instructions in the same chat. OpenAI’s example: ask ChatGPT to watch a project board for new tasks, and when one arrives it reads the linked documents and drafts a plan. The developer docs add others, such as watching a feedback channel for bug reports and opening draft pull requests with fixes, or applying review comments left on a document. OpenAI is building this on a proposed MCP Events specification, and plugins need to support MCP 2.0 for it to work. Discovery Finding and building plugins For developers, Plugin Creator helps build a plugin, and a redesigned submission flow gives clearer feedback. For everyone else, OpenAI says improved ranking and recommendations will surface relevant plugins in the directory and inside conversations. You still choose which plugins to use and approve the access each one gets. Plugin permissions are shared across ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, Codex and dots, and you manage plugin access in ChatGPT’s Plugins tab. OpenAI says its plugin ecosystem connects to over 4,000 apps . FAQs Do I need to install anything to get extensions? No. Extensions come through the plugins you use, once their developers add support. Composer mentions work only in the ChatGPT desktop app, and extensions on the web are coming soon to Free and Go. Can a plugin act without me asking? With MCP events, ChatGPT acts on a plugin’s updates only after you ask it to watch for them, and you choose what it monitors and what it does. A dot can also read from your connected apps in the background, but those research tools are read-only and can’t send messages or change app content. Can Sites use plugins too? Yes, on Business, Enterprise, Healthcare and Edu plans. You can add supported plugins to a Site that’s private to your workspace, if the feature is enabled, and each teammate uses it with their own connected data and permissions. Related

817decab-fa08-45e9-84ba-b7007093050f.title: Olight Unveils ArkTac Series and New ArkPro Ultra Colorway at O-Fan Day 2026
817decab-fa08-45e9-84ba-b7007093050f.incipit: Olight, a global innovator in portable lighting, unveiled the ArkTac Series at O-Fan Day 2026, bringing ArkPro's signature flat-body, multi-source design to tactical lighting for the first time. The company also introduced Amber Orange for ArkPro Ultra, alongside several new portable-lighting products. Launc
817decab-fa08-45e9-84ba-b7007093050f.body: /CNW/ -- Olight, a global innovator in portable lighting, unveiled the ArkTac Series at O-Fan Day 2026, bringing ArkPro's signature flat-body, multi-source design to tactical lighting for the first time. The company also introduced Amber Orange for ArkPro Ultra, alongside several new portable-lighting products. Launching during National Preparedness Month, the new releases reflect Olight's focus on helping users stay prepared, from fast response to everyday readiness. Olight unveils the new ArkTac Series and ArkPro Ultra in Amber Orange at O-Fan Day 2026 "The best products start with understanding how people really live, and our O-Fans have always been an important part of that journey," said Mavis Xiao, general manager at Olight. "As we come together for our fifth in-person O-Fan Day, we're grateful for a community that continues to share its ideas and feedback with us. That connection keeps us focused on real-world needs, from the new ArkTac Series to Amber Orange ArkPro Ultra." ArkTac Series: All-In-One Tactical Versatility Inspired by ArkPro's flat-body, multi-function design, the new ArkTac Series brings that approach to handheld tactical lighting. Available in two models, ArkTac and ArkTac Ultra, the series combines an easy-to-carry flat profile with immediate tactical controls and multiple light sources. Designed for fast, intuitive control, a two-stage tail switch provides immediate access to Turbo Spotlight and Pure Flood without cycling through modes. The new CommandPoint shortcut activates Strobe with one touch by default and can be customized for other frequently used functions. Both models also feature UV and Red Light, while ArkTac Ultra adds a Green Laser. The series delivers up to 1,800 lumens and reaches up to 215 meters. ArkTac Ultra also debuts OAL2, the next generation of Olight's proprietary aluminum alloy. It delivers 7.3% greater hardness and 11.5% higher yield strength than first-generation OAL. ArkPro Ultra Amber Orange: Crafted to Stand Out As the premium model in the ArkPro Series, ArkPro Ultra debuts in Amber Orange, its most vibrant color yet. Warm and energetic, the new colorway is designed to stand out, bringing the high visibility associated with outdoor and emergency equipment to everyday carry. Rich metallic orange contrasts with sleek black accents, while polished edges catch the light to reveal shifting highlights and a refined sense of depth. This layered finish is achieved through a dual-anodizing process -- a first for Olight -- that also offers up to twice the scratch resistance of Olight's standard anodized finishes. Beyond its new look, ArkPro Ultra combines premium design with everyday-carry versatility, keeping preparedness close at hand. Its signature flat design brings together four light sources -- Pure Flood, Spotlight, UV and Green Laser -- with seven lighting configurations. Featuring Olight's self-developed EIP 1 LED, ArkPro Ultra delivers up to 1,700 lumens in a compact EDC flashlight. Also unveiled at O-Fan Day were the PL X GL, Oclip 2 Series and Marauder 3. Pricing and Availability ArkPro Ultra Amber Orange, PL X GL and Marauder 3 will be available September 21 for $129.99, $149.99 and $369.99, respectively. The Oclip 2 Series will also be available September 21, starting at $49.99. The ArkTac Series, starting at $119.99, is expected later this year. Pricing and availability may vary by market. About Olight Founded in 2007, Olight is a global innovator in portable lighting, offering high-tech solutions for everyday carry, outdoor, tactical and professional use. With over 1,200 patents and international recognitions, including the iF Design Award and Red Dot Design Award, Olight products are available in more than 100 countries worldwide. dda3a579-e08d-4081-9c63-87dc643d7e23.title: Ferrari 296 Speciale and Lamborghini Revuelto Meet To See Which Reigns Supreme in the PHEV World
dda3a579-e08d-4081-9c63-87dc643d7e23.incipit: The Ferrari 296 Speciale and Lamborghini Revuelto are probably the world’s most impressive plug-in hybrid supercars. The V12 and the three electric motors of the Revuelto make it far heavier, while the 296...
dda3a579-e08d-4081-9c63-87dc643d7e23.body: The Ferrari 296 Speciale and Lamborghini Revuelto are probably the world’s most impressive plug-in hybrid supercars. The V12 and the three electric motors of the Revuelto make it far heavier, while the 296 Speciale is low on power, but also on weight. So which one reigns supreme in the plug-in-hybrid supercar world? They both look like they eat SUVs and crossovers for breakfast. They both come from worlds of performance. And they are both electrified. They sound like the perfect rivals, but are they really that similar at the end of the drag strip? The Ferrari 296 Speciale is powered by a plug-in system that integrates a 3.0-liter twin-turbocharged V6, working alongside a single, Formula One-derived MGU-K (Motor Generator Unit, Kinetic) dual-rotor electric motor. Together, they produce 868 horsepower (880 metric horsepower) and 557 pound-feet (755 Newton meters) of torque. Those are enough to make it rocket from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 2.7 seconds, run the quarter mile in 10.2 seconds with a trap speed of 151 mph (243 kph), and max out at 205 mph (330 kph). A Formula One-derived, eight-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission puts the power through the rear wheels with the help of an electronic differential. Photo: Carwow | YouTube The plug-in hybrid system has to push forward 3,109 pounds (1,410 kilograms). A high-performance track-focused braking system, with massive carbon-ceramic ventilated discs, controlled by an advanced electronic brake-by-wire system, provides the stopping power. In the meantime, its Lamborghini-badged rival, the Revuelto, rolled off the production line in Sant’Agata Bolognese with a plug-in hybrid setup that integrates a 6.5-liter V12 with naturally aspirated firepower and three electric motors, with two mounted on the front axle, independently driving the four wheels, and one integrated directly into the rear-mounted eight-speed dual-clutch auto box. The system pumps out 1,001 horsepower (1,015 metric horsepower) and 783 pound-feet (1,062 Newton meters) of torque. It makes the Revuelto rocket from 0 to 60 in 2.3 seconds, which is 0.4 seconds quicker than the Ferrari 296 Speciale , run the quarter mile in just 9.4 seconds at 146 mph (235 kph), and top out at 218 mph (350 kph). An eight-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission throws the power to the pavement in an all-wheel-drive setup. The Revuelto, with its three electric motors, weighs more than the 296 Speciale: 3,907 pounds (1,772 kilograms), but has way more power and all-wheel drive. So which one is it going to be the winner that takes it all? Photo: Carwow | YouTube Because there is only one way to determine the fastest of Maranello’s and Sant’Agata Bolognese’s plug-in hybrids, Mat Watson of Carwow took both to the track and let them race. Which is the absolute king down the straights, and which brakes better? The Ferrari 296 Speciale: Base MSRP starts at $475,364, while the Lamborghini Revuelto is a $608,358 deal in America, before options and taxes. Due to Ferrari's Atelier/Tailor Made programs and Lamborghini's Ad Personam customization, heavily optioned builds (adding carbon fiber packages, custom paint, and titanium components) routinely inflate the final window sticker by $100,000 to $200,000. Because production slots for these hyper-hybrids are heavily restricted, early-delivery vehicles on the used exotic market carry massive premiums. For example, the first pre-owned 296 Speciale models entering the US market have seen asking prices as high as $1.9 million. Joe is the owner of the Ferrari. He has just bought the car and has already taken it to the racetrack. He’s got less power on his hands but also less weight, and that is what he is counting on. He surely wins the attention race: his Ferrari is finished in purple, which Ferrari calls Viola 51, and features racing stripes in Rosso Corsa, while the Lamborghini wears what seems to be the Nero Nemesis. Photo: Carwow | YouTube Mat drives the Lamborghini Revuelto, while Joe handles his own car, the Ferrari 296 Speciale. On the first pass, the Revuelto rockets off the line and seems to be powerful enough to win. But the 296 Speciale immediately makes up for the lost time and ground for what seems to be a photo finish. The roll race down the half mile is up next. They start in the sportiest drive mode (the Qualify for the Ferrari and the Corsa for the Lamborghini) and are ready to launch at 30 mph (48 kph) in third gear. This time, it is the Ferrari’s turn to behave like a land rocket right from the get-go, leaving Mat Watson horror-struck. What has just happened? They try a roll race starting in second gear, as Mat hopes that his turbos will kick in at the right time. His strategy works and puts him in the lead, while it is Joe's turn to try to keep up in his plug-in hybrid purple Ferrari. Then, to test the hybrid torque, they launch from 50 (80 kph) or 60 mph (97 kph) in eighth gear. At launch, Mat waves goodbye to Joe as he leaves him behind and unable to recover, so the Lambo wins again to crown itself the king of the roll races. Photo: Carwow | YouTube Then, Mat and Joe switch to manual mode. Once again, the extra power that the Lamborghini comes with puts it in the lead, despite the heavier frame. But Mat has to admit: that 296 Speciale looks great in his rearview mirror. Joe complains his gearbox shits strange. However, Mat loses the braking test, as his Lamborghini pays tribute to the extra weight. History repeats itself in the next roll race, as it is a photo finish once again. But the cameraman saw it best: it was the Ferrari the winning car. Mat shoots ahead in the second race, but the Ferrari builds up speed and makes up for the lost ground, for a photo finish again. But the numbers are quite relevant. The Lamborghini Revuelto took 10.0 seconds for the quarter mile, while the Ferrari needed 10.2 seconds for the run. At the end of the day, it is next to impossible to pick the winner. The Lamborghini Revuelto is far more powerful, but it is also the heavier of the two, while the Ferrari 296 Speciale shows that it is always brain over brawn. Liked the article? ffbb7535-57dc-43c9-9096-24b3bee23ae0.body: iQOO's gaming-focused small tablet is now official. Meet the iQOO Pad Ultra. It comes with an 8.8-inch AMOLED screen with 2304x1440 resolution (for a 16:10 aspect ratio), a 165Hz refresh rate, and 4,500-nit peak local brightness (peak full-screen brightness is 1,600 nits). Like the iQOO 16 , which also launched today , the iQOO Pad Ultra is powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset. iQOO has also packed its self-developed Q4 gaming chip into the tablet, as well as its Wi-Fi enhancement chip. The device comes with an active cooling fan too. iQOO Pad Ultra official images On the rear there's a 13MP camera, while on the front there's an 8MP one. The Pad Ultra has a 9,020 mAh battery with support for 66W wired charging. It runs Android 17 with OriginOS 7 on top. The iQOO Pad Ultra boasts symmetrical dual speakers, two X-axis linear vibration motors, RGB lights on the back, and a metal unibody construction. It will be available in silver and black. More iQOO Pad Ultra official images It starts at CNY 5,999 (approximately $890) with 12GB of RAM and 256GB of storage, until October 6, when it goes up to CNY 6,499 ($964). The 16/256GB model is priced at CNY 7,199 ($1,068). You need to shell out CNY 7,999 ($1,187) for the 16/512GB option, and the range-topping 16GB/1TB model will set you back CNY 8,999 ($1,335).
